summary: Preview OpenAPI 3.2.0 wire-shape contracts for HR, payroll, and accounting foundation flows.

findings: Contracts define only the paths backed by current Rust DTO/app/domain flows, avoiding speculative service-wide endpoint sprawl.
Each artifact explicitly records preview-not-deployed status and non-claims instead of implying a live runtime.
OpenAPI surfaces are per-microservice and versioned as openapi-v1.yaml with semver metadata, preserving independent service evolution.
Using OpenAPI 3.2.0 aligns to the latest official OpenAPI specification rendering checked on 2026-05-23.

F3_adversarial.failing_fixture_id: api-semver metadata checks for each contracts directory
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Validation fails if version suffix metadata is absent, version major mismatches v1, required metadata fields are empty, or related ADRs are missing.
findings: JSON/YAML structural parse passes for all three OpenAPI artifacts.
oya gate validate api-semver passes for HR, payroll, and accounting contract directories.
OperationIds map directly to business actions and x-oyatie-app-function points at the Rust app-layer functions.
Consistent ApiErrorEnvelope and tenantBearer security scheme help later adapter authors keep handlers uniform.
Structural parse and api-semver gates passed before evidence closeout.
No new Rust dependencies, crates, runtime frameworks, or generated code were introduced in this slice.

alternatives_named: defer wire contracts until runtime adapter implementation
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Hand-authored preview OpenAPI gives future cloud/runtime adapters a stable reviewable wire target without adding generator dependencies or runtime coupling.
rejected_reasons: Deferring would leave later HTTP work to invent wire shapes under runtime pressure.
Generation would require adding or selecting tooling beyond this evidence scope.

findings: Contracts require tenant/legal-entity/evidence identity fields and define bearer security scheme metadata, while explicitly not claiming runtime enforcement.
No secrets, listeners, clients, databases, filing transports, or payment rails were added.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: No deployed API runtime exists for these services; no latency or throughput claim is made.

findings.summary: Static contract artifacts add no runtime path.

findings: x-data-class metadata marks PII and FINANCIAL fields in the contract surfaces.
Non-claims state that compliance certification, statutory filing, and runtime access control are outside this preview contract slice.
Additive contract and metadata files can be removed with the spec AC-08/decision-log rows and task plan entries. No code or data migration exists.
Contracts define audit evidence and idempotency-related response metadata but emit no logs, traces, metrics, or audit records at runtime.
The artifacts are initial preview v1 contracts and carry semver metadata before any public deployment, reducing future migration ambiguity.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: Wire contracts are useful before cloud integration only if they are explicit previews with semver metadata and runtime non-claims.
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Later runtime adapters would lack reviewed endpoint, schema, and version metadata, increasing accidental contract drift.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Waiting for deployed HTTP runtime would mix contract review with auth, routing, infrastructure, and SLO evidence.

findings: Fits API-first microservice sequencing: domain/app/API DTO crates now have a matching versioned wire-contract review surface.
Contract files follow existing microservices/*/contracts/openapi-v1.yaml naming and semver metadata convention.
Plan, todo, and specs document the OpenAPI preview contract slice and non-claims.
Artifacts live under each microservice contracts directory, matching existing repository contract layout patterns.
No runtime adapter, router, auth middleware, storage, Workflow client, or filing transport was introduced.
Static OpenAPI/metadata files add no Rust or third-party dependencies.
HR, Payroll, and Accounting specs gained AC-08 OpenAPI acceptance refs pointing to semver-validated contract files.
No algorithmic runtime path exists; schema patterns mirror the deterministic DTO/domain validation prefixes and digest shapes.
